# Bug report

Hello all,
I was cross compiling python 3.9.15 (which is actually the latest [stable release](https://www.python.org/downloads/source/)) for riscv64 linux architecture on ubuntu 22.04 LXC container and ubuntu 20.04 on host machine and found out that upon execution of `make`, it terminates with following error:
```
if test $? -ne 0 ; then \
        echo "generate-posix-vars failed" ; \
        rm -f ./pybuilddir.txt ; \
        exit 1 ; \
fi
/bin/sh: 1: python: not found
generate-posix-vars failed
make[1]: *** [Makefile:618: pybuilddir.txt] Error 1
make[1]: Leaving directory '/home/runner1/python_on_riscv/Python-3.9.15'
make: *** [Makefile:547: profile-opt] Error 2
```
# Reproducing the Error:

My configuration command for Makefile was:
```
# It does not make any difference whether or not to use --enable-optimizations
./configure --host=riscv64-unknown-linux-gnu --build=riscv64-unknown-linux --prefix=$PREFIX --disable-ipv6 ac_cv_file__dev_ptmx=yes ac_cv_file__dev_ptc=yes --enable-optimizations
```
After this, the `Makefile` produced will have variable `PYTHON_FOR_BUILD` with `python` instead of `python3.9` (or whatever it should be). Complete variable definition in `Makefile` is as follows:
```
PYTHON_FOR_BUILD=_PYTHON_PROJECT_BASE=$(abs_builddir) _PYTHON_HOST_PLATFORM=$(_PYTHON_HOST_PLATFORM) PYTHONPATH=$(shell test -f pybuilddir.txt && echo $(abs_builddir)/`cat pybuilddir.txt`:)$(srcdir)/Lib _PYTHON_SYSCONFIGDATA_NAME=_sysconfigdata_$(ABIFLAGS)_$(MACHDEP)_$(MULTIARCH) python
```
After this, executing `make -j$(nproc)` will produce the error described above.


# Environment

<!-- Include as many relevant details as possible about the environment you experienced the bug in -->

- CPython version 3.9.15 tested on: cross compiled with riscv64-unknown-linux-gnu-* toolchain from [here](https://github.com/riscv-collab/riscv-gnu-toolchain)
- Operating system and architecture: Ubuntu focal (and jammy on LXC Container) Intel x86 64-bit

# Possible Fix
**>>> Correct me here if I am wrong**  
Replacing python with python3 solves the problem. I am mentioning this based on my observation for python 3.8.15. In my case python 3.8.15 builds without any issue. Also replacing `python` with `python3.9` in Makefile does not solve the above mentioned problem while cross compiling for riscv64 linux with `riscv64-unknown-linux-gnu`.  
If there is some other bug or if I am doing something wrong feel free to mention.

# UPDATE:
## Update 1:
This is issue is also coming on python3.8 on ubuntu22.04 running on lxc container. Also one important thing to mention is that the variable `PYTHON_FOR_REGEN` is set to python3 and when building the same version and source files on ubuntu 20.04 running on x86_64 this variable is set to python3.8 and builds fine on x86_64 host machine.
  
Here is the output of `diff Makefile Makefile_ssh` (Makefile_ssh is the one taken from lxc container running ubuntu22.04 ):
```
33,34c33,34
< abs_srcdir=	/home/ali/python_on_riscv/python3.8.15
< abs_builddir=	/home/ali/python_on_riscv/python3.8.15
---
> abs_srcdir=	/home/runner1/python3.8.15
> abs_builddir=	/home/runner1/python3.8.15
200c200
< OPENSSL_LIBS=-lssl -lcrypto
---
> OPENSSL_LIBS=
250,252c250,252
< PYTHON_FOR_REGEN=python3.8
< UPDATE_FILE=python3.8 $(srcdir)/Tools/scripts/update_file.py
< PYTHON_FOR_BUILD=_PYTHON_PROJECT_BASE=$(abs_builddir) _PYTHON_HOST_PLATFORM=$(_PYTHON_HOST_PLATFORM) PYTHONPATH=$(shell test -f pybuilddir.txt && echo $(abs_builddir)/`cat pybuilddir.txt`:)$(srcdir)/Lib _PYTHON_SYSCONFIGDATA_NAME=_sysconfigdata_$(ABIFLAGS)_$(MACHDEP)_$(MULTIARCH) python3.8
---
> PYTHON_FOR_REGEN=python3
> UPDATE_FILE=python3 $(srcdir)/Tools/scripts/update_file.py
> PYTHON_FOR_BUILD=_PYTHON_PROJECT_BASE=$(abs_builddir) _PYTHON_HOST_PLATFORM=$(_PYTHON_HOST_PLATFORM) PYTHONPATH=$(shell test -f pybuilddir.txt && echo $(abs_builddir)/`cat pybuilddir.txt`:)$(srcdir)/Lib _PYTHON_SYSCONFIGDATA_NAME=_sysconfigdata_$(ABIFLAGS)_$(MACHDEP)_$(MULTIARCH) python
1952a1953
>
```

Took me a while to figure it out. So here is the solution:  
**For cross compiling python, you should have the same version of python installed on your machine first.**.
For example if machine has 3.10 and you are cross compiling 3.9, then it will not work !
